maven-org-codehaus-plexus-plexus-utils-2.impact: None. The vulnerable method is present and nothing in the application or the build calls it.
maven-org-codehaus-plexus-plexus-utils-2.fix_expected: Merged into flow main on 2026-10-07. It is not in a Vaadin release yet.

maven-io-netty-family-not-reached.impact: None for a production application without Control Center that makes no reactor-netty calls of its own. Otherwise the code handles traffic with the servers your own client calls, or with your Kubernetes API server.
maven-io-netty-family-not-reached.workaround: Set <netty.version>4.1.139.Final</netty.version> in the pom that inherits spring-boot-starter-parent. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.4.26, 24.7.17, 24.9.24 and 24.10.12: it moves every io.netty artifact to 4.1.139.Final, which osv.dev lists clean. That measures resolution, not compatibility, so run your tests. If your pom only imports spring-boot-dependencies, the property does nothing and you manage the io.netty artifacts in your own dependencyManagement instead, which was not measured here.
maven-io-netty-family-not-reached.fix_expected: Spring Boot decides this version, not Vaadin. No free Spring Boot release a Vaadin 24 line declares pins a fixed netty: 3.2.12, 3.4.13 and 3.5.16, the newest of their lines on 2026-10-24, pin 4.1.115.Final, 4.1.130.Final and 4.1.135.Final. It arrives when Spring Boot raises netty.version; until then, the property.

maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.impact: Every Vaadin 24.4 and 24.7 application on the embedded Tomcat. Most of the nine need a Tomcat feature a Spring Boot application does not configure by default (FORM or DIGEST authentication, DataSourceRealm, security-role-ref, the rewrite valve, unix domain sockets); CVE-2026-73180 is about WebSocket sessions outliving the HTTP session, and Vaadin push uses WebSocket.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.workaround: Add <tomcat.version>10.1.61</tomcat.version> to the properties of your pom. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.4.26 with Spring Boot 3.2.12 and on 24.7.17 with 3.4.13: tomcat-embed-core, tomcat-embed-el and tomcat-embed-websocket move to 10.1.61. Only resolution was measured, not a running application. Remove it when you move to a Spring Boot that pins a fixed Tomcat.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.fix_expected: None from Spring Boot 3.2 or 3.4 on Maven Central, which ends those lines at 3.2.12 and 3.4.13, pinning 10.1.33 and 10.1.50; later releases are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support.

maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.impact: Every Vaadin 24.4 and 24.7 application on the embedded Tomcat, which is the default of the starter.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.workaround: Add <tomcat.version>10.1.61</tomcat.version> to the properties of your pom. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.4.26 with Spring Boot 3.2.12 and on 24.7.17 with 3.4.13: tomcat-embed-core, tomcat-embed-el and tomcat-embed-websocket move to 10.1.61. maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.fix_expected: None from Spring Boot 3.2 or 3.4 on Maven Central, which ends those lines at 3.2.12 and 3.4.13; later releases are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support.

maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.impact: None through Vaadin or Spring on the 24 series. Your own code that parses a DataInput with Jackson is a separate question.
maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.workaround: None needed, unless your own code parses a java.io.DataInput with Jackson.

maven-org-springframework-spring-websock.impact: None unless the application uses the Spring WebSocket module itself, since Vaadin own push uses Atmosphere rather than this module. Where it does, a predictable session identifier lets an attacker guess a session that belongs to somebody else.
maven-org-springframework-spring-websock.workaround: Set the spring-framework.version property in your own pom to 6.2.19, which the advisory database reports clean for this artifact, and take it out once you move to a Spring Boot that pins it itself. maven-org-springframework-spring-websock.fix_expected: No further Spring Boot 3.4 release will arrive on Maven Central: the line ends there at 3.4.13, and later releases, 3.4.18 today, are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support. The version only moves when you set it or when you move to a newer Spring Boot.

maven-com-vaadin-flow-maven-plugin-2026-.impact: None in the deployed application. On 24.4 and 24.7 a build whose frontend step fails prints every environment variable of that build, which on a continuous integration service is often readable by more people than the secrets were meant for.
maven-com-vaadin-flow-maven-plugin-2026-.workaround: Keep secrets out of the environment the Maven build runs in, passing them another way, and restrict who can read build logs. No property turns the logging off.
maven-com-vaadin-flow-maven-plugin-2026-.fix_expected: No release of 24.4 or 24.7 is announced with the fix. Flow 24.4.21 and 24.7.18, published to Maven Central on 2026-10-21 and not yet in a Vaadin release, still declare the library.

maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.impact: None unless you add tomcat-coyote-ffm yourself and run CLIENT_CERT authentication with soft fail disabled on an FFM connector.

maven-io-netty-netty-transport-native-kq.fix_expected: Spring Boot decides this version, not Vaadin. maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.workaround: On 24.7, <spring-framework.version>6.2.19</spring-framework.version> clears CVE-2026-41848; on 24.4 the same property resolves and clears it too, but moves Spring Boot 3.2 onto a Spring Framework minor it was not built for, so test it first. The fixes for the other six exist only in Broadcom's commercial releases, so nothing you can download clears them on any 24 series.
maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.fix_expected: The releases that fix these, spring-core 6.1.29 and 6.2.20, are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support, and the 2026-11-19 Spring cycle moved that stream on to 6.1.30, 6.2.21 and Spring Boot 3.5.18: Maven Central still ends the free lines at 6.1.21, 6.2.19 and Spring Boot 3.5.16 and answers 404 for all three of the newer ones, read on 2026-11-20.

maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.impact: None unless one of your own types bound from browser JSON uses one of those features, or copilot runs in production. maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.workaround: If one of your types meets a condition above, set <jackson-bom.version>2.18.12</jackson-bom.version> on 24.4 and 24.7, or <jackson-bom.version>2.21.7</jackson-bom.version> on 24.9 and 24.10, in the properties of your own pom. maven-org-springframework-boot-actuator-.impact: None unless the application runs Actuator and declares an endpoint requiring authentication under a health group additional path or under /cloudfoundryapplication. There a request to that endpoint is served without authentication.
maven-org-springframework-boot-actuator-.workaround: Move any authenticated endpoint of your own out from under the paths set in management.endpoint.health.group.<name>.additional-path and out from under /cloudfoundryapplication.
maven-org-springframework-boot-actuator-.fix_expected: Vaadin 24.9 and later declare Spring Boot 3.5.16, which carries both fixes. No 3.4 release you can download will: Maven Central ends that line at 3.4.13, and the later 3.4 releases are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support.

maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.impact: None. Neither the examples web application nor the clustering code is on your classpath through Vaadin.

maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.impact: None unless the application registers UrlHandlerFilter with very broad patterns, or maps UrlFilenameViewController with an end of path pattern and no prefix. There a crafted link redirects to another site.
maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.workaround: If you register UrlHandlerFilter, give it narrow patterns; if you map UrlFilenameViewController, configure a prefix. The 6.2 release that fixes either, 6.2.20, is commercial from Broadcom, so raising the version from your pom cannot reach it.
maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.fix_expected: Fixed on Maven Central only in Spring Framework 7.0.9, which needs Spring Boot 4 and so Vaadin 25. maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.impact: None unless the application has disabled, expired or locked users, and even there what an attacker learns is which usernames those are. It discloses account state, not passwords.
maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.workaround: Set <spring-security.version>6.5.11</spring-security.version> in a pom that inherits spring-boot-starter-parent. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.7.17: all seven Spring Security artifacts move from 6.4.13 to 6.5.11 and spring-core stays at 6.2.15, the same 6.2 line 6.5.11 is built against. maven-io-projectreactor-netty-reactor-ne.impact: None. No Reactor Netty server is ever created, so nothing listens for the requests the advisory describes.

maven-ch-qos-logback-logback-core-24-7.impact: Every Vaadin 24.7 application, since logback is the logging backend Spring Boot configures by default. All three are low, and all three are reached through logback own deserialisation and class instantiation machinery rather than through ordinary logging calls: an application that does not enable a socket receiver and does not let untrusted input reach its logback configuration has no path to them.
maven-ch-qos-logback-logback-core-24-7.workaround: Set the logback.version property in your own pom to 1.5.38, the newest of that line, which the advisory database reports clean, and take it out once you move to a Spring Boot that pins a fixed logback itself. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.7.17 against Spring Boot 3.4.13: it moves logback-core and logback-classic together from 1.5.22 to 1.5.38, and slf4j-api stays at 2.0.17.
maven-ch-qos-logback-logback-core-24-7.fix_expected: No further Spring Boot 3.4 release will arrive on Maven Central: the line ends there at 3.4.13, and later releases, 3.4.18 today, are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support. The version only moves when you set it or when you move to a newer Spring Boot.

maven-org-springframework-spring-web-24-.workaround: Set the spring-framework.version property in your own pom to 6.2.19, which the advisory database reports clean for this artifact, and take it out once you move to a Spring Boot that pins it itself. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.7.17 against Spring Boot 3.4.13: it moves spring-core, spring-beans, spring-context, spring-web, spring-webmvc, spring-websocket and spring-expression together from 6.2.15 to 6.2.19.

The version only moves when you set it or when you move to a newer Spring Boot.

maven-org-bouncycastle-bcprov-jdk18on-24.impact: None unless your own code performs FrodoKEM decapsulation, either through BouncyCastlePQCProvider or by calling FrodoKEMExtractor directly. Nothing Vaadin, Control Center or Spring puts on a 24.7 classpath does either. Where it is reached, the time the decapsulation takes leaks what the algorithm is meant to keep secret, which is why the advisory scores confidentiality high; its own CVSS v4 vector records the exploit maturity as unproven.
maven-org-bouncycastle-bcprov-jdk18on-24.workaround: None needed for this advisory. If you already applied the bcprov-jdk18on 1.85 override that answers the other four advisories on this jar, it clears this one too: osv.dev reports nothing at all against 1.85, asked on 2026-11-06.
maven-org-bouncycastle-bcprov-jdk18on-24.fix_expected: No Vaadin 24.7 release will move the version, because Control Center is no longer developed. The 24.9 and 24.10 lines pin a Control Center that resolves bcprov-jdk18on 1.85, and an application that does not declare control-center-starter resolves no Bouncy Castle on 24.7 at all.

maven-io-projectreactor-netty-reactor-ne.impact: None unless your own code makes reactor-netty client requests that carry credentials and follow redirects.
maven-io-projectreactor-netty-reactor-ne.workaround: If your own code does, on 24.7 set <reactor-bom.version>2024.0.18</reactor-bom.version> in the pom that inherits spring-boot-starter-parent. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.7.17: it moves reactor-netty, reactor-netty-core and reactor-netty-http from 1.2.13 to 1.2.18 and reactor-core from 3.7.14 to 3.7.19. On 24.4 the 1.1 line has no fix; the same property, measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.4.26, moves reactor-netty to 1.2.18 and reactor-core from 3.6.12 to 3.7.19, a Reactor generation Spring Boot 3.2 never shipped, so test it before you rely on it. Both measure resolution, not compatibility.
maven-io-projectreactor-netty-reactor-ne.fix_expected: Fixed upstream in 1.2.18 and 1.3.6; osv.dev records 1.1.31 as the last affected 1.1 release, so no 1.1 release fixes it. Spring Boot 3.2.12 and 3.4.13, the newest free releases of the lines 24.4 and 24.7 declare, pin Reactor 2023.0.12 and 2024.0.13, so no Vaadin or Spring Boot release will move it there. 24.9 and 24.10 resolve 1.2.18.

If your pom only imports spring-boot-dependencies, the property does nothing and you manage the io.netty artifacts in your own dependencyManagement instead, which was not measured here.
maven-io-netty-netty-codec-http2-unreach.fix_expected: Spring Boot decides this version, not Vaadin. maven-com-vaadin-vaadin-2026-2742-stale-.impact: None on 24.7.16 and later. Below it, a request to a reserved path creates a session without authentication.
maven-com-vaadin-vaadin-2026-2742-stale-.workaround: On a release below 24.7.16, upgrade to Vaadin 24.7.16 or later; 24.7.17 is the newest.

npm-minimatch-globparts-24.impact: None unless your own build code passes a glob pattern that someone outside your team can choose to glob or minimatch. There, a crafted pattern makes the build spend excessive CPU and memory.

maven-org-springframework-boot-spring-bo.impact: None unless the application persists sessions to disk, registers the PID file writer, or uses ${random.value} where a secret is needed, and in the first two cases only against an attacker who already has a local account on the host.
maven-org-springframework-boot-spring-bo.workaround: Leave server.servlet.session.persistent at its default of false, do not register ApplicationPidFileWriter, and replace any ${random.value} used as a secret with a value you generate and store yourself. Moving to Spring Boot 3.5.14 or newer fixes the first two in the framework.
maven-org-springframework-boot-spring-bo.fix_expected: None from the 3.4 line on Maven Central, which ends at 3.4.13: the later 3.4 releases are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support, and the advisory database marks the line affected up to 3.4.15 or 3.4.16 with no fixed release. The fixes are on 3.5.14 and 3.5.15, which are published, so the way out is a newer Spring Boot. Vaadin 24.9 and later declare 3.5.16.

npm-glob-abort-signal-24.impact: None unless your own build code passes an AbortSignal to glob to limit a walk. There, the walk keeps reading the file system after it was cancelled.

maven-org-springframework-spring-webmvc-.impact: None from Vaadin. For an application that renders XsltView under a /** mapping, CVE-2026-47884 is remote code execution: the verdict is that Vaadin does not create the condition, not that the condition is harmless.
maven-org-springframework-spring-webmvc-.workaround: If you render XSLT views, name the view explicitly rather than letting the mapping derive it from the request path. Raising the Spring Framework version from your pom does not help: the 6.1 and 6.2 releases that carry the fix exist only under Broadcom's commercial Spring support.
maven-org-springframework-spring-webmvc-.fix_expected: Fixed publicly only in Spring Framework 7.0.9, which needs Spring Boot 4 and so Vaadin 25. spring.io marks 6.2.20 and 6.1.29 Enterprise Support Only.

maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.impact: None unless a Vaadin 24 application declares observability-kit-starter and whoever can send a baggage header can reach it. There it is a denial of service through memory and CPU, not a way in.
maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.workaround: With Spring Boot, set <opentelemetry.version>1.62.0</opentelemetry.version> in your pom; take it out once your Spring Boot pins 1.62.0 or later. Without Spring Boot that property moves nothing, because only Spring Boot's dependency management reads it: import io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-bom 1.62.0 in dependencyManagement. Do not declare observability-kit-starter 3.2.1 yourself on 24.4 or 24.7: since 3.2.0 its license listener extends a Flow class that first ships in flow-server 24.9, the listener is a registered service init listener, and the application fails at startup with NoClassDefFoundError. In every case resolution was measured, not compatibility with Observability Kit. If you do not use baggage, otel.propagators=tracecontext drops the baggage propagator instead. These moves change the jar your application resolves and not the copy inside the Observability Kit agent, which carries its own: the 3.2.1 and 4.1.2 agents carry OpenTelemetry 1.62.0 and 1.65.0, both past this one, and the 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 agents carry 1.23.0 and 1.44.1, which are not.
maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.fix_expected: With Spring Boot, on 24.4 and 24.7 none from any Spring Boot you can download: Maven Central ends those lines at 3.2.12 and 3.4.13, which pin 1.31.0 and 1.43.0, and later releases are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support. On 24.9 and 24.10 a Spring Boot 3.5 patch pinning 1.62.0, which does not exist yet: 3.5.16, the newest open one, pins 1.49.0. Without Spring Boot, 24.9 and 24.10 already resolve 1.62.0 through Observability Kit 3.2.1 and need nothing, and on 24.4 and 24.7 the exit is an Observability Kit release built for those lines, a 3.1.1 from the 3.1.0 tag carrying a fixed OpenTelemetry, and a platform release pinning it on both branches. Kit 3.2.1 and later cannot be that release: they fail at startup on any Flow before 24.9.

maven-org-apache-logging-log4j-log4j-api.impact: None. The artifacts the two advisories are about are not resolved by the application.

maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.impact: None unless the application has configured CLIENT_CERT authentication on a connector backed by Tomcat Native, with soft fail disabled. There a request that should have been rejected for a bad client certificate can be accepted.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.workaround: Upgrade Tomcat Native to 1.3.7 or 2.0.14 if you use it, which is where the advisory puts the fix on that side. On the Tomcat side the property tomcat.version set to 10.1.61 moves it, as the other Tomcat verdict on these series records.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.fix_expected: None from any Spring Boot you can download: the advisory names Tomcat 10.1.53 as the fix, Spring Boot 3.2.12 and 3.4.13, the last releases of their lines on Maven Central, pin 10.1.33 and 10.1.50, and later Spring Boot releases are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support.

maven-org-apache-commons-commons-lang3-c.impact: None unless the application runs Commons Text or Commons Configuration interpolation over untrusted input. There a long class name stops the thread with an Error that most code does not catch.
maven-org-apache-commons-commons-lang3-c.workaround: With spring-boot-starter-parent, set <commons-lang3.version>3.18.0</commons-lang3.version> in the properties of your pom. Without that parent, declare org.apache.commons:commons-lang3 3.18.0 in your dependencyManagement. Measured on 2026-10-24: the property moves 24.4.26 on Spring Boot 3.2.12 from 3.13.0 to 3.18.0 and 24.7.17 on Spring Boot 3.4.13 from 3.17.0 to 3.18.0, and the dependencyManagement entry moves 24.4.26 to 3.18.0 as well. That measures resolution, not compatibility.
maven-org-apache-commons-commons-lang3-c.fix_expected: No Spring Boot release you can take on these lines carries it. The newest of 3.2 and 3.4, 3.2.12 and 3.4.13, pin 3.13.0 and 3.17.0, and the newest 3.5, 3.5.16, pins 3.17.0.

maven-io-netty-netty-codec-memcache-2026.impact: None through netty-codec-memcache. Read the findings on the artifact each advisory actually names, in particular netty-codec-http and netty-handler, which a Vaadin 24 application does resolve and which carry real advisories at these versions.

npm-highcharts-2026-107588-24-7.impact: None on Vaadin 24.7.16 and later. On earlier 24.7 releases, chart options that carry data an attacker controls can run script in the viewer's browser or pollute Object.prototype, as each advisory describes.

npm-vite-dev-server-2026-10-22.impact: None in a deployed application. On a developer machine, two of the launch-editor advisories need Windows and the third needs an editor such as Vim or Emacs and a file named with a leading plus or minus sign.
npm-vite-dev-server-2026-10-22.workaround: Upgrade within your line where a release carries the fix: 24.10.12 resolves vite 7.3.7, 25.2.12 and 25.3.3 resolve 8.3.4. An overrides entry for launch-editor changes nothing, because vite compiles it into its own files.
npm-vite-dev-server-2026-10-22.fix_expected: Not on 23.6, 24.4, 24.7 or 24.9 yet. Vaadin names vite exactly, so a rebuilt lockfile never takes a fix on its own: 24.9.24 still pins 7.3.6 and 24.7.17 pins 6.4.3, one patch below 7.3.7 and 6.4.4, published 2026-10-06, and the 3.2 and 5.4 lines that 23.6 and 24.4 pin have no fixed release.

maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.impact: None from three of them unless polymorphic typing is enabled on your ObjectMapper, where they instantiate unexpected classes, CVE-2026-110879 being the incomplete fix follow-up of CVE-2026-54512 with the same condition. maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.impact: Any Vaadin 24.7 application secured with Spring Security: responses can go out without the headers it should add, for example letting sensitive pages be cached.
maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.workaround: Set <spring-security.version>6.5.11</spring-security.version> in a pom that inherits spring-boot-starter-parent. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.7.17: all seven Spring Security artifacts move from 6.4.13 to 6.5.11 and spring-core stays at 6.2.15, the same 6.2 line 6.5.11 is built against. That is resolution, not a running application. Remove it once your Spring Boot pins 6.5.11 or later. Without upgrading, Spring documents calling setShouldWriteHeadersEagerly(true) on the HeaderWriterFilter through an ObjectPostProcessor in your security configuration.
maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.fix_expected: Vaadin 24.9 and later resolve Spring Security 6.5.11. The 6.4 fix, 6.4.15, is commercial only and Maven Central ends 6.4 at 6.4.13.

maven-org-springframework-security-saml2.impact: None through Vaadin. The SAML module is not resolved, so the relying party registration and response decryption code the three advisories name is not on the classpath.

maven-org-springframework-retry-spring-r.impact: None unless the application uses stateful retries through spring-retry, which in a Vaadin application means Control Center or a retry setup of your own. There the cache grows until the application runs out of memory.
maven-org-springframework-retry-spring-r.workaround: Set the spring-retry.version property in your own pom to 2.0.13, which the advisory database reports clean.
maven-org-springframework-retry-spring-r.fix_expected: Spring Retry 2.0.13 is already published, so nothing has to be waited for. Vaadin releases do not pin this version, Spring Boot does, and its 3.4 line ends at 3.4.13 on Maven Central, with later releases published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support.

maven-com-vaadin-vaadin-core-2026-2742-s.impact: None on 24.7.16 and later. Below it, a request to a reserved path creates a session without authentication.
maven-com-vaadin-vaadin-core-2026-2742-s.workaround: On a release below 24.7.16, upgrade to Vaadin 24.7.16 or later; 24.7.17 is the newest.

maven-io-netty-netty-codec-haproxy-unrea.impact: None for a production application without Control Center that makes no reactor-netty calls of its own. Otherwise the code handles traffic with the servers your own client calls, or with your Kubernetes API server.
maven-io-netty-netty-codec-haproxy-unrea.workaround: Set <netty.version>4.1.139.Final</netty.version> in the pom that inherits spring-boot-starter-parent. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.4.26, 24.7.17, 24.9.24 and 24.10.12: it moves every io.netty artifact to 4.1.139.Final, which osv.dev lists clean. That measures resolution, not compatibility, so run your tests. If your pom only imports spring-boot-dependencies, the property does nothing and you manage the io.netty artifacts in your own dependencyManagement instead, which was not measured here.
maven-io-netty-netty-codec-haproxy-unrea.fix_expected: Spring Boot decides this version, not Vaadin. Vaadin 24.9.19, 24.10.8 and later declare Spring Boot 3.5.15 or 3.5.16, which pin 4.1.135.Final and carry these fixes. On 24.4 and 24.7 the newest free Spring Boot of the line, 3.2.12 and 3.4.13, pins 4.1.115.Final and 4.1.130.Final, so no release will move it there; the property is the way.

npm-opentelemetry-core.impact: None without an application that extracts baggage headers from incoming requests.

maven-org-springframework-data-spring-da.impact: None unless the application has its own MVC controllers or Hilla endpoints that accept Pageable, Sort or projections. There an attacker exhausts the heap or the stack with crafted property paths.
maven-org-springframework-data-spring-da.workaround: The 3.2 and 3.4 releases carrying the fix are commercial from Broadcom, not on Maven Central. Setting <spring-data-bom.version>2025.0.13</spring-data-bom.version> moves it to 3.5.13, which osv.dev reports clean; that is the Spring Data generation of Spring Boot 3.5, so test your own repositories on it before shipping.
maven-org-springframework-data-spring-da.fix_expected: The releases the advisories name as fixed, 3.4.15 and later than 3.2.15, are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support; Maven Central ends those lines at 3.4.13 and 3.2.14, read on 2026-10-24. Vaadin 24.9 and later resolve 3.5.13, which is clean.

maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.impact: None unless the application builds its own token service on KeyBasedPersistenceTokenService. There an attacker who can submit tokens repeatedly learns the expected value one character at a time from how long each rejection takes.
maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.workaround: If your code declares a KeyBasedPersistenceTokenService, compare the token yourself with java.security.MessageDigest.isEqual, which does not return early. There is no property to set.
maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.fix_expected: No free release for Vaadin 24. Maven Central ends 6.4 at 6.4.13 and 6.5 at 6.5.11, both in range, and the open source fixes, 7.0.7 and 7.1.1, need Spring Boot 4. Setting spring-security.version to 6.5.11 on 24.7 does not change this.
